ARMED BY #579 and unkillable IN THE CANONICAL ENVIRONMENT: promoted into the window by comment exclusion. The site is `NEWER_FLAG=-newermB`, whose value is immediately overwritten with `-newer` on any platform whose find rejects birth-time comparison. ubuntu-latest ships GNU find, which does, so the mutated value never reaches the real find call and no assertion can see it. Kill verdicts are only comparable in that environment (docs/testing.md), so this cannot be closed by a test. CI evidence: dispatched full sweep on this branch, run 32181527467 (ubuntu-latest, SKIP_STRESS=1).

ARMED BY #579 and unkillable IN THE CANONICAL ENVIRONMENT: promoted into the window by comment exclusion. The site is the self-referential `find -newermB` PROBE that decides BSD-vs-GNU. GNU find rejects `-newermB` and `-eqwermB` alike, so the probe's non-zero status — and therefore NEWER_FLAG=-newer — is identical with and without the mutant on ubuntu-latest. CI evidence: dispatched full sweep on this branch, run 32181527467 (ubuntu-latest, SKIP_STRESS=1).
